_doc.artifact: nodb repo index template (Phase 4 Gate A) -- the create-index body.
_doc.ported_from: modules/core/core-repo/src/main/resources/com/enonic/xp/repo/impl/repository/index/{settings,mapping}/default/search-{settings,mapping}.json (Elasticsearch 2.4.6). Those files are UNTOUCHED: this is a nodb-path-only port, so embedded ES keeps its layout byte-identical and no existing install needs a reindex.
_doc.engine: OpenSearch 3.7.0, STOCK opensearchproject/opensearch:3.7.0 -- analysis-icu is NOT required (D8: the 44 icu_collation filters were its only consumer; the 2 remaining filters and all 38 language analyzers are core Lucene, with ja/ko/zh on core `cjk`).
how_it_is_applied: NoDB PUTs `<tenant>-<repo>+g<N>` with `settings` + `mappings` from this file plus a computed `aliases: {"<tenant>-<repo>": {}}`. A composable index template cannot carry a per-index alias, so the alias is attached in the create call.

`settings.index.number_of_replicas` and `settings.index.refresh_interval` are substituted from cell config at create time (OpenSearchConfig). Everything else is identical across environments so analysis is environment-independent.

`mappings._meta.templateVersion` travels into the live index, so a generation can be asked which template built it. A template change is a new generation (`+g(N+1)` rebuild + alias flip), never an in-place mutation.

divergences_from_the_es_layout_and_why._text: D1/BLOCKER 1. StaticIndexValueType.STRING has postfix "", so XP emits a BARE field alongside its dotted sub-fields -- and OpenSearch expands dots into objects, so `data.x` would have to be a leaf AND an object at once. It fires on the FIRST document of every repo. The nodb path gives the text value type the postfix `_text`, completing the nine-postfix public vocabulary (text is the only one whose postfix was empty). NOTE: OpenSearch's `text` means ANALYZED, so XP's `_text` maps to an engine `keyword` -- a vocabulary collision, not an error (XP's `_fulltext` is itself an engine `text` field).
divergences_from_the_es_layout_and_why._fulltext: D1b. The index-config directive is `fulltext`, the query function is `fulltext()`, the dynamic template was already NAMED template_fulltext -- only the physical field said `_analyzed`. Renamed on the nodb path at zero incremental cost since D1 already moves the resolver table.
divergences_from_the_es_layout_and_why.path_match: BLOCKER 2. All 91 ES templates use `match: "*._analyzed"`, which after dot-expansion matches the LEAF name (`_analyzed`) and therefore NEVER fires: index create succeeds, indexing succeeds, and queries return zero hits with no error anywhere. Every template here uses `path_match`, and DynamicTemplateFiringTest proves it with a real indexed document and a real query rather than by inspection.
divergences_from_the_es_layout_and_why._orderby_<loc>: D8. Was `type:string, index:analyzed, analyzer:icu_sort_<loc>` and sorted on directly (legal in ES 2.4 only because fielddata was on by default). NoDB now computes the ICU collation key itself (CollationKeyResolver, hex-encoded, icu4j pinned in nodb's version catalog) and stores a plain `keyword`, so: no fielddata, no icu_collation_keyword, no analysis-icu plugin, 44 filters + 44 analyzers deleted (settings 600 -> ~60 lines), and 44 templates collapsed into ONE. The engine's own icu4j (77.1 in the image) never touches the sort contract.
divergences_from_the_es_layout_and_why.standard_token_filter: REMOVED in OpenSearch and present in 6 XP analyzers. Deleted here. This is a BEHAVIOUR change, not a syntax fix (it was already a no-op in late ES 2.x); Gate D's corpus is what proves the token streams still match.
divergences_from_the_es_layout_and_why.document_index_default_vs_fulltext_searc: These two are BYTE-IDENTICAL in search-settings.json (same custom/standard/lowercase+asciifolding+word_delimiter chain), i.e. there is no index/search asymmetry to preserve. Both names are kept (the mapping and, from Gate D, query-time analyzer selection reference them by name) but they are one analyzer. Consequence worth documenting: because asciifolding is in the chain, `fulltext()` IS accent-insensitive while the raw `_text` field is NOT -- proven by corpus row UNTYPED-05-ascii-folding -> 0 hits. That asymmetry is behaviour, not a bug.
divergences_from_the_es_layout_and_why.default_search: search-mapping.json sets `search_analyzer` ONLY on `*._ngram`. Everything else falls back to the index-level default search analyzer, which is what the analyzer literally named `default_search` IS (a reserved name, in ES 2.4 and in OpenSearch alike). Preserved exactly: the fulltext/path templates deliberately do NOT set an explicit search_analyzer. Gate 0(d)'s draft did, and flagged it as a behaviour change -- this port does not take it.
divergences_from_the_es_layout_and_why.bare_untyped_string_mapping: Settled BY MEASUREMENT, not reasoning (Gate 0(e), 10 UNTYPED-* corpus rows in ES mode): exact multi-word value 1 hit, single token of it 0 hits (NOT tokenized), case-differing 1 hit (lowercased), punctuation preserved, ASCII folding 0 hits (NO folding), over-ignore_above 0 hits (not indexed), LIKE prefix works. That is exactly `keyword` + a lowercase normalizer + ignore_above -- which is also what template_metadata_strings' `keywordlowercase` analyzer did. So `_text` (and the catch-all) map to keyword/keywordlowercase/ignore_above:3072 -- XP's OWN 3072, not the 8191 the Gate 0(d) draft guessed.
divergences_from_the_es_layout_and_why._all: `_all` and 91 `include_in_all: false` deleted (removed in ES 6). XP has its own `_allText`, so nothing is lost; `all_field_analyzer` was `_all`'s only consumer and is deleted with it.
divergences_from_the_es_layout_and_why._default_: The `_default_` mapping-type wrapper is gone (mapping types removed). With it goes the "a new branch inherits the templates" trick -- which is moot here because branch is no longer a mapping type but an ordinary `_branch` keyword field, and one index holds every branch of a repo.
divergences_from_the_es_layout_and_why.normalizer: `ignore_above` is illegal on `text`, legal on `keyword`. Porting the 47 `ignore_above` fields to keyword needs a `lowercase` NORMALIZER, which does not exist anywhere in XP's settings today (only the analyzer of the same name) and is authored here.
divergences_from_the_es_layout_and_why.edge_ngram: `edgeNGram` -> `edge_ngram`. `"side": "front"` is DROPPED: it is silently ACCEPTED and inert in Lucene 10 (front is the only behaviour), and silent acceptance is worse than rejection.
divergences_from_the_es_layout_and_why.dates: Explicit `format` on `*._datetime` -- OpenSearch date parsing is stricter than 2.4's. The wire ships epoch millis (proto int64), which is exactly the precision an ES 2.4 `date` stored, so `epoch_millis` is listed first.
divergences_from_the_es_layout_and_why.limits: `total_fields.limit` 1000 (OpenSearch's default; ES 2.4 had none) -> 10000, because dot expansion means every path SEGMENT is an object mapper that now counts too -- 3 properties can be 10 leaves but 15 mappers. `depth.limit` 20 -> 50 for the same reason. `max_result_window` pinned at the 10000 XP already lives with rather than left implicit.
divergences_from_the_es_layout_and_why.catch_all_must_exclude_objects: FOUND AT GATE A, third blocker of the same family as Gate 0's two, and only findable by indexing a real document. ES 2.4's `match: "*"` matched LEAF field names, so template_metadata_strings was harmless. `path_match: "*"` matches every PATH -- including the object nodes that dot expansion creates (`data`, `data.title`, `_path`, `_permissions`). The catch-all then maps `data` as a keyword and EVERY document fails: `failed to parse field [data] of type [keyword] ... Can't get text on a START_OBJECT`. Fix: `match_mapping_type: "string"` on the catch-all -- `object` is one of the values match_mapping_type can take, so naming a leaf type is what excludes objects. Note it takes a SINGLE value in OpenSearch 3.7, not the array ES 8 accepts (`No field type matched on [[string, long, double, boolean]], possible values are [object, string, long, double, boolean, date, binary]`). Consequence, and an improvement over parity rather than a gap: a NON-string leaf that no postfix template claims now falls to OpenSearch's own dynamic default (long stays long) instead of being coerced to a string the way ES 2.4's template_metadata_strings did. Under D1 there are no such leaves -- every field XP emits ends in a postfix -- so no behaviour changes; the catch-all is purely a safety net. Louder than blocker 2 (it errors rather than returning zero hits) but it fires on the FIRST document of every repo, exactly like blocker 1.
divergences_from_the_es_layout_and_why.reserved_metadata: `_id` and `_source` are rejected outright as document fields by OpenSearch (ES 2.4 tolerated both). NodeIndexPath declares both, but NodeStoreDocumentFactory never emits them; the projection rejects them defensively rather than trusting that.

deferred: `nested_fields.limit` left at its default 50 -- the V1 layout uses no nested fields (DESIGN §5 roadmap).

`index.search.idle.after` (default 30s, new since 2.4) stops background refresh on an idle index and makes the next search block. Harmless for correctness because §3.3's contract is checkpoint + explicit refresh, but it makes first-query latency after idle lumpy.

`_allText` has no `_text` base variant (createAllText emits only ANALYZED + NGRAM + stemmed), so its concatenated text still sits in _source twice. Making it a multi-field halves the largest field in the index -- additive, DESIGN §5 'Virtual / derived fields', not a parity item.
ja/ko/zh are on core `cjk`, a bigram analyzer materially weaker than kuromoji. The managed service preinstalls kuromoji, so improving this later costs no infrastructure change.
